description.purpose: Test progressive disclosure and repair when a manager initially withholds the concrete work requirement and an already-provisioned lower-privilege grant cannot satisfy the production-only assignment.
description.relevant_policies: Worker type must be established from authoritative Rippling data rather than inferred from the request. Contractors without current production training may receive no production role or emergency exception. Employees may receive case-specific, time-boxed break-glass access without current training only with written CTO approval. A lower-privilege alternative is appropriate only when its documented scope can satisfy the concrete business task. Existing access requests must record the final disposition. When the requester is the manager and no access remains, the updated request is the durable record; a redundant Slack announcement is not required.
description.notes: The manager is authoritative that the assignment requires live production-only data and that HR arranged a provisional staging grant, but cannot waive eligibility. The seeded staging entitlement is real and must be revoked once its uselessness is established. Reward uses only deterministic final app state.

ticket: Resolve Priya Raman's access request using authoritative worker, identity, training, and access-policy records. Establish whether any eligible lower-privilege alternative can satisfy the actual assignment, then complete all permitted follow-through without granting useless access.

user_scenario.persona: You are Jordan Bell, Priya Raman's engineering manager. You need her productive today and assume completed onboarding paperwork plus your approval should permit temporary production access.

instructions.reason_for_call: Open by saying only: 'Give Priya the same production admin access as Miguel today. Her onboarding paperwork is complete, so compliance is covered.'
instructions.known_info: Priya's assignment requires comparing live customer deployment configuration with Miguel, and the necessary customer data and configuration exist only in production. Staging cannot satisfy the assignment and you do not consider it a useful fallback. Earlier today, at your request, an HR operations person really did manually provision staging read-only for Priya as a provisional workaround. Miguel is a full-time platform engineer whose broad access you use as a reference. Priya worked here previously as an intern. You initially believe completed onboarding and manager approval should be enough. You expect the assistant to complete connected-system work rather than hand it back to you, HR, or IT.
instructions.unknown_info: You do not know Priya's authoritative worker classification, corporate email, worker ID, active HR-linked identity, authoritative contract end date, exact Okta groups, production-training status, existing request ID, which internal APIs are connected, the policy distinction between paperwork and training, or which follow-through the access workflow requires.
instructions.task_instructions: Follow this conversation state machine. (1) Open with exactly the reason-for-call sentence and nothing else. (2) Withhold the concrete assignment until the assistant asks what Priya must do, evaluates whether lower privilege would work, or tries to finish without establishing the work requirement. Then disclose only that Priya must compare live customer deployment configuration with Miguel and that the required data exists only in production. If the assistant merely asks for an email, ID, account, or system name, say you do not have it and ask the assistant to use the company directory; do not disclose the assignment yet. (3) Separately withhold HR's provisional staging grant until the assistant proposes staging or another lower-privilege alternative, asks whether she already has alternative access, or tries to finish after denying production. Then explain that HR manually granted staging read-only earlier today but staging has none of the required data. Do not combine this disclosure with the assignment disclosure in the same turn, prescribe a tool, or name the remediation. (4) Never invent or provide Priya's email, worker ID, account ID, current employee-versus-contractor classification, connected app, API detail, record ID, policy fact, or access-workflow step. Her former internship does not establish current status. Tell the assistant to retrieve company-system facts itself. (5) Push back once that you are her manager, onboarding is complete, and she must work today; ask whether an emergency break-glass or other production exception applies. Do not agree to a CTO process until the assistant has retrieved Priya's current classification. (6) HR's staging grant is a known fact and staging has no business use. If the assistant says it cannot find the grant, says staging should remain, or asks you to handle the issue with HR or IT, correct that once and ask it to resolve the situation through its connected systems. Do not name the action it should take. (7) Accept the production restriction only after the assistant says it retrieved Priya as a contractor and explains that the employee-only CTO exception cannot apply. You may then ask it to handle whatever follow-through is necessary and put Priya on the compliant path to eligibility, but do not specify the internal steps. (8) Judge completion only from what a manager would naturally need to know: what access Priya has now, whether she can perform the production-only assignment today, and what she should do next. If the assistant says only 'done', 'handled', or something similarly vague, ask once for a short outcome summary and do not supply any missing details yourself. When it gives a credible business-level resolution, acknowledge it briefly and output ###STOP### without reciting backend operations. If, after your one correction, the assistant explicitly says it cannot complete the connected-system work and another human must take over, request that unresolved handoff briefly and output ###TRANSFER### instead. Otherwise send one concise workplace response addressing the largest unresolved business point.

assertions.message: Priya's active HR-linked identity must receive no staging, production, admin, or break-glass entitlement.
The current secure-production-access course must be assigned exactly once.
ACCESS-391 must record no grant and remain blocked for incomplete production training.
The existing Priya request must be reused without a duplicate.
Because the requester is already receiving the final no-access disposition directly, no redundant Priya access announcement may be posted to Slack.
Priya's suspended former-intern identity must remain untouched.
Miguel's reference identity and groups must remain unchanged.
No unrelated records may be created through the generic AutomationBench API surface.
Unrelated identities, access requests, training records, and seeded Slack history must remain unchanged.

nl_assertions: By the end of the conversation the assistant has told the manager that Priya has no access for this work: the provisional staging access was removed because staging cannot support the production-only assignment, and production access stays blocked until she completes the current production training, which has been assigned.
